finding.title: Chat asks 'Do you want me to start a session ...?' with no card, and a yes gets 'Yes to what?'
finding.what_the_person_sees: After 'sounds good': 'Do you want me to start a session on Garden club (up to CHF 1)?' with no Yes/No card. A following 'ok' or 'yes' gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.', which also does not say how to start.
finding.expected: Either the chat's question can be answered with yes (a read-back card), or the reply says how to start ('press Start or say run it now'). Step: each reply says what happens next.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/c17-chat.json ('sounds good', 'ok'), c17-chat-b.json ('yes' -> 'Yes to what? ...'; 0 sessions)
finding.repro: Project with ready tasks and no open card: say 'sounds good', then 'yes'.
finding.suspected_cause: The parser answers a bare yes before the chat model sees the conversation, so a yes to the model's own question is lost.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is real. The evidence is out of order, though. In c17-chat.json the 'ok' that got 'Yes to what?' came before 'sounds good', and it followed a 'No' to a card, not the model's question. In c17-chat-b.json the 'yes' followed a softer invitation ('...or say if you want a session started.'), not the exact 'Do you want me to start ...?' question. The code still explains the claim, and it reproduces exactly on the stand-in. Bench v4s2, --provider bench, run through POST /chat: two ready tasks, then 'say: ... Do you want me to start a session on Garden club (up to CHF 1)?', then 'yes'. The reply was 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.', the chat model call count stayed at 1, and no session started. 'ok' after 'say if you want a session started' got the same reply.

Causes:
(1) agent.ts:1215-1220 answers any bare yes or ok before the chat model is called, unless a card is pending or liveOffer() finds the app's own Go-ahead offer. liveOffer() (agent.ts:893-896) only knows reply.offer.action === 'go_ahead'. Nothing looks at whether the model's newest reply asked the person a question. isYes (wiring/state-ports.ts:213) counts 'ok' as a yes.
(2) The app's own words: YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (agent.ts:527) says nothing about what happens next or how to start. LC-C17 requires that each reply says what happens next.
(3) The prompt the app sends makes the model's choice likely. evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:20-21 tells the model that '"yes" ... refer to' its earlier replies, which promises that a yes reaches it. Nothing tells it not to end with a yes/no question, or that a session start is offered by calling the start command (read back once) or by telling the person to say 'run it now' or press Start.

The app follows design §3.9 ('"yes" with no card ("Yes to what?")'), but that rule did not foresee the chat model asking a question in prose.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1215 (bare-yes guard; liveOffer at :893, YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY at :527); evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:20-21
verdict.fix_sketch:
Two parts, both small.

(a) Runtime (agent.ts:1215): when the newest turn is a model answer (no notice, no card, no actions) that ends in a question, send a bare yes or ok on to the model with the history instead of answering 'Yes to what?'. The model then calls session_start, which already gets the D6 read-back 'Start a session on <project> (up to CHF N)? [Yes] [No]' (askFromChat), so nothing starts without the card's Yes. Keep 'Yes to what?' for a yes after a notice, a command sentence or an answered card. Update design §3.9 and runtime.md to say this.

(b) Words: give YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY a next step, e.g. 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes. Say what you want done, for example "run it now" to start a session.' Add a prompt rule (conversation-agent.md, bump the version): never ask the person a yes/no question in prose. To offer a change, call its command, which the runtime reads back. To offer a start, say "say 'run it now' or press Start". Fix the line that says 'yes' refers to earlier replies.

The prompt rule alone would leave the runtime gap, so do (a) as well.

finding.title: The dependency change's reply does not say when the task runs
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'make the FAQ wait for the README', Yes -> '"Write the FAQ" now waits for "Write the README".' [Undo]
finding.expected: Each reply says what happens next (step), as the add-a-task reply does ('It runs at your next Start.').
finding.evidence: c17-chat.json line 7 afterAnswer; screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/19-c17-23-answered-yes.png
finding.repro: Chat: 'make the FAQ wait for the README', then Yes.
finding.suspected_cause: task.dependencies' done sentence has no next-step clause.

verdict.root_cause: After the Yes, the reply is the task.dependencies command's own sentence. The model does not write it. The command's run() builds that sentence from dependenciesSentence() plus an optional note clause and nothing else. It never calls withNextLine/prepareWork, and it adds no wait clause. withNextLine (task.ts:1656-1670) is called only by task.create (:991), task.transition to ready (:1318), task.resume (:1474) and task.reopen (:1547). The area's S-9 decision listed only "the commands that make a task ready" as ones that get the next-step line, so task.dependencies was left out. Two plan texts still expect the line here. ADR 0118 point 3 (docs/decisions/0118-who-starts-a-session.md:57-65) puts "a chat change" among the things that prepare work and say a line. LC-C17 (runC-plan live_check_4) and the planned §3.9 text ("every other change only prepares work and its reply says what happens next") expect it too. The sentence the person saw is pinned word for word by packages/runtime/test/chat-steering.test.ts:103 and apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:4327. I re-ran the chat-steering case at 4cf11fd and it passes, so the code produces exactly what the person saw. Adding a dependency to a ready task leaves it waiting. prepareWork would return nothing_to_run with no line for it, so the missing clause has to be a wait clause such as "It runs after X is done, at your next Start." The finding does not mention a related case with the same cause, which is stronger: "let the FAQ run on its own" (depends_on: []) makes a waiting task runnable. That reply ('"Write the FAQ" waits for no other task now.') also says nothing about when it runs, and the command prepares no work. ADR 0118 point 3 covers that case directly.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:2010 (task.dependencies run sentence; dependenciesSentence at :1913-1917; withNextLine at :1656 not called)
verdict.fix_sketch: In taskDependencies.run, after setDependencies, re-read the task. (1) If it is ready and its dependencies are all done (for example after the last dependency was removed), return withNextLine(ctx, outcome, task). That calls prepareWork, which lets the task join a running session if it fits, and appends afterMove(line): "It runs at your next Start." / "It joins the session that is running." / the no_room line. (2) If it still waits on dependencies that are not done, append a wait clause built from ctx.ports.previewWork, which is read-only: 'It runs after "Write the README" is done, at your next Start.' With a running session it should say '..., in this session if budget is left, else your next Start.' Name only the dependencies that are not done yet, and keep the line under 100 characters. Optionally give the read-back the same preview, as withPreview does for moves. Then update the pinned sentences: chat-steering.test.ts:103, real-daemon.test.ts:4327, tasks.test.tsx:1022 (the drawer's Change what it waits for shows change.sentence) and the fake daemon's sentence (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts:3188). Also update design §3.9 and ADR 0118 point 3 so they say a dependency change states when the task runs.

Start with two ready tasks, "Write the README" and "Write the FAQ", and no session running. Say "make the FAQ task depend on the README task", then "yes". Expect the reply '"Write the FAQ" now waits for "Write the README". It runs after it is done, at your next Start.' Then say "let the FAQ run on its own", then "yes". verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine (S-9: every preparing action says what happens next; ADR 0118 point 3 names a chat change)
verdict.notes: Not the model alone: the reply after Yes is the command's deterministic sentence, the same with and without a model. This is a gap in the spec as it was built, not a regression. S-9 deliberately listed only the commands that make a task ready, while ADR 0118 point 3 and LC-C17 say every chat change. Severity stays at words. The sentence is true, and the header shows the right count: "Ready: 2 tasks wait for your Start" after the change. The earlier add-a-task reply had already said "It runs at your next Start." The case that weighs more is the dependency removal, because it makes a task runnable. ADR 0118 point 3 promises that this case prepares work, yet the command never calls prepareWork. No leftover file (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) names task.dependencies or a dependency change's next-step line. finding.title: On the real fast model, chat mostly skips recall and says recorded things do not exist
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'There is no README task in Quote Page's task list ... The nearest is "Write the deploy notes" ... If you meant an earlier task with that name, I can search the records for it.' / 'I can't see a licence choice in what I have for Quote Page ... I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?' / 'I haven't set any budget in this conversation' (chat itself replied 'I set the budget to CHF 2.00.') / 'I found no record of you saying anything else about the logo in this conversation' ('Das Logo bleibt dunkelblau' is recorded) / 'I can't see a merge date for the README ... Should I do that?' / in Recipe site: 'There was no card about the first page in this project, so there is nothing we said about one.'
finding.expected: The chat prompt says 'Look it up before you say you do not have it'. The user guide says 'Chat looks up what Forerunner recorded when the answer is not in front of it'. LC-C10 passes when the right record is named with its date in at least 10 of 12 past questions and no reply says a recorded thing is missing.
finding.evidence: c10-quote.json and the model-call log: in Quote Page 1 of 11 past questions called recall (06:10:36, recall {kinds:[sessions], from 2026-11-09, to 2026-11-15}); the others were single Haiku calls with no tool. Score: 3 of 12 right with date, 4 right without date, 5 'not there'. With 'search the records: when was the README merged?' recall found it: 'The README was merged on Tue 10 Nov. The task was called "Write the README" then'. In Bakery 2 of 2 past questions called recall and were right.
finding.repro: Seed recall-home into a bench-live home (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/scripts/seed-recall.mts), open Quote Page's Chat and ask 'what happened to the README task?', 'which licence did we choose?', 'what did I say about the logo?', 'what did you set the budget to?' and 'when was the README merged?'.
finding.suspected_cause: claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low treats the turn's context (# Tasks with current titles, lessons, doc excerpts, the last 12 turns) as complete. Nothing in code makes a lookup before a 'not found' answer; the rule is in the prompt only.

verdict.root_cause:
The design makes looking things up entirely the model's choice, and the model the app picks for chat (claude-haiku-5-5, effort low, thinking off) mostly does not look. The model-call log (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl) confirms it: recall and recall_open were offered in all 37-tool requests, but in Quote Page only seq 7 (p3, 'last week') called recall. Every other past question was a single end_turn call with no tool. Two things in the app make that choice likely and leave it unchecked.

(1) The prompt the app sends gives the model a way out. conversation-agent.md:14 says 'You answer fast and short from what you are given'. :38 lists the lookup tools as tasks_list, task_get, session_last and files_list, without recall. :68 says 'If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through', and the replies follow that shape exactly ('Nothing in its tasks, open questions or the last session mentions one. I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look...?'). CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) opens with 'The first message holds what is true now: this project's tasks...' and 'Answer questions about now from the first message without a lookup'. To a low-effort model, 'what happened to the README task?' and 'which licence did we choose?' read as task-list questions about now.

(2) No code backstops the rule. agent.ts:2029-2090 guards only claims that something changed or that a yes was asked for (claimOf/claimNudge, the l3-chat-claims fix for the same kind of live miss). Nothing compares a 'not there / can't find / I found no record / should I look?' reply with the turn's recall calls. The facts' task lines (agent.ts:2914) also carry only current titles, so the renamed task ('Write the README', now 'Write the guide') is invisible without recall. That accounts for p2, p9 and x1.

Retrieval itself works. recall-rank.test.ts (the golden set on the same recall-home fixture, including the README, merge date, licence, logo and budget questions) passes at 4cf11fd. The explicit 'search the records: ...' and 'yes, look it up' turns found the right records.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:14, :38, :68; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:617 (CHAT_RECALL_RULES, a rule in the prompt only); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2029-2090 (guards change claims only, not absence claims); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2914 (task facts with current titles only)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. A code backstop beside the claim guard, in ConversationAgent.chat at agent.ts about 2029-2090, built like claimOf/claimNudge:
   - Add absenceOf(text) in claims.ts. It matches English and German absence or offer-to-search wording: 'there is no', 'I can't see/find', 'I found no record', 'nothing ... mentions', 'I haven't searched', 'Should I look', 'keine ... gefunden', 'nicht gefunden'.
   - When the turn offered recall and called neither recall nor recall_open, nudge once within CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS with a RECALL_NUDGE text: 'You said it is not there without looking it up. Call recall now with the person's words and other words for it (an earlier name, another language), then answer. Never ask whether to look.' Use the step line 'Looking it up…' and do not stream the reply that triggered the nudge.
   - If there is still no lookup, code runs recall with the line's words (as the stand-in's recallWords does) and either hands the hits to one more step or replaces the reply with what was looked through.
   - Log the guard on the chat.reply row.
2. The prompt (conversation-agent.md 1.4.1, CHAT_RECALL_RULES asserted verbatim again):
   - Line 14: '...from what you are given and what you look up'.
   - Line 38: add recall and recall_open to the lookup tools.
   - Line 68: 'If what you were given does not hold the answer, look it up with recall in this turn; if recall finds nothing, say what you looked through.'
   - CHAT_RECALL_RULES: add 'Never offer to search or ask whether to look: look it up in this turn. A question about a task, decision, card, document or something said that the first message does not answer needs a lookup.'
3. Cheap, deterministic: a task line in the facts names an earlier title from the change_log, e.g. '"Write the guide" (earlier "Write the README"): Merged', so a renamed task is answered from now.

verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-recall
verdict.notes:
Checked against the evidence. The model-call log shows recall offered on every call and called once in 11 past questions in Quote Page. In Bakery the model did call it, 2 of 2: the model looks when a question names a time or a card answer, and skips when the facts hold something nearby (the task list, a doc excerpt, a lesson).

Two parts of the score come partly from the fixture.
- p8 (budget): the seeded reply 'I set the budget to CHF 2.00.' was written with actions [] (testenv/src/bench/recall-home.ts:111, :476-489), so by the prompt's own 'The app did:' rule that reply changed nothing. It had also scrolled out of the 12-turn window. So 'nothing has changed' is half right; 'I haven't set any budget in this conversation' is still a false statement about what chat said.
- p7 (logo): the content came out right (dark blue, from the lesson and docs/brand.md). The false part is 'I found no record of you saying anything else', said without a search.

Clear misses: p2, p6, p9, plus x1 and x3. x3 is the hosting decision 'Where is the page published? Only as a local file for now', which is recorded and was not looked up.

The model's own replies say 'I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look?', so it saw the tool and chose to ask. That is why I hold the prompt's competing wording and the missing guard responsible, not the model alone. A 'yes' to that offer then gets 'Yes to what?'; that is a separate finding (likely L4-chat-2).

No leftover names this. CL-11 (leftovers-C2) only says 'LC-C10 watches the real model's choice', and it is about ranking and which hit gets opened.

finding.title: 'yes' to chat's own question is answered 'Yes to what?'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Chat: 'I haven't searched the earlier conversation and decisions yet. Should I look for it?' Person: 'yes'. Chat: 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' Same after 'This plan needs the stronger model, which costs more and asks you first. Should I go ahead?'.
finding.expected: A yes to the question chat just asked does what the question offered: it looks the record up, or shows the stronger model's ask with Go ahead. Otherwise chat should not end a reply with a yes/no question it cannot take a yes to.
finding.evidence: c10-follow.json f1 (0 model calls, 219 ms); c13b.json e2; screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png shows 'yes' / 'Yes to what?' under the model's 'Should I go ahead?'.
finding.repro: In a chat where Haiku answers 'Should I look for it?' (e.g. ask 'which licence did we choose?' in Quote Page), type 'yes'.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts around line 1215: a bare 'yes' with no read-back card and no live offer gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY and never reaches the model. The model is free to end replies with its own yes/no questions.

verdict.root_cause: ConversationAgent.chat answers every bare yes itself, before any model call, whenever the app has nothing of its own waiting: no read-back card, and no app-made go_ahead offer on the newest reply. The check is `else if (this.deps.commands && isYes(req.text) && !liveOffer(earlier)) return finish(await this.nothingWaitingReply(earlier), …)`. `liveOffer` (agent.ts:893-896) only knows `reply.offer.action === "go_ahead"`. `nothingWaitingReply` (:2592-2605) only knows `pendingId`. A question the model writes into its own reply text ("Should I look for it?", "Should I go ahead?") is invisible to both, so the yes gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (:527) with 0 calls. The app's own prompt makes those questions likely and promises the model it will see the yes: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md says '"It", "that", "yes" … refer to them [your earlier replies]' and tells voice to offer "more?". The facts' thinking_longer line "asks the person first" (agent.ts:1721, depth.ts thinkingLongerFact) led Haiku to write its own ask line in d2 and e1 without calling answer_thoroughly, so only the generic Think-it-through offer was attached and no go_ahead existed. The design line "'yes' with no card ('Yes to what?')" (core-experience.md:254) was written for a chat whose only questions were the app's cards. With the model now asking its own questions, the reply "Nothing is waiting for your yes" sits right under a visible question, which breaks §5 rule 4 (true now). Reproduced on the stand-in: a FakeProvider reply ending "Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?", then "yes", gives exactly YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY with provider.calls = 1 (/tmp/frbench/l4chat2/yes.test.ts, passes at 4cf11fd). The live evidence matches: c10-follow f1 has 0 calls in 219 ms, and c13b e2 has 0 calls. Typing "yes, look it up" (f2) gets past the isYes regex, and the model then does the right thing (recall, then the answer).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1215
verdict.fix_sketch: At agent.ts:1215, a bare yes goes to the model, with its history, when the newest turn is a model answer that ends with a question and has nothing of the app's on it: not a notice, no pendingId, no actions, no go_ahead offer. Keep "Yes to what?" (and the answered-elsewhere and expired lines) only when the newest reply asked nothing. One way to do this is a helper `modelAsked(earlier)` that checks the newest reply's text without its read-back with /\?\s*$/, used as `isYes(req.text) && !liveOffer(earlier) && !modelAsked(earlier)`. This is safe: a yes that reaches the model still cannot change anything without a command, and every change is read back ("A question in reply is not a yes"; the claim guard). The model then does what it offered: it calls recall, or it calls answer_thoroughly, which gives the app's real ask line with figures and Go ahead. Also: (a) reword the thinking_longer 'asks' fact so it tells the model to call answer_thoroughly and let the app ask, for example "asks the person first: call answer_thoroughly; the app asks under your answer", so the model stops writing its own "Should I go ahead?"; (b) optionally add to conversation-agent.md: "Do not end with an offer to look something up: look it up." Mirror the rule in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts:4428, and update docs/design/core-experience.md §3.9 and user-guide.md:400 ("yes" with no card and no question from chat).
verdict.failing_test_idea: Runtime composed test (conversation-memory.test.ts or chat-recall.test.ts), with an apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts case through POST /projects/:id/chat. The stand-in answers "which licence did we choose?" with "I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?". Then "yes" is posted. Expect a second model call whose messages hold that question and the "yes", the stand-in calling recall, and the reply being its found answer, not YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (fails today: the reply is "Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes." with 1 call). Second case: the stand-in writes "This plan needs the stronger model … Should I go ahead?" with no tool call. "yes" then reaches the model, the model calls answer_thoroughly, and the reply ends with the app's ask line and Go ahead. Keep as regressions: "yes" after a plain statement reply, and "yes" with nothing before it, still give YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY with 0 calls. "yes" under a waiting card still answers the card.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth (owns the typed-yes path for offers: liveOffer, acceptedOffer and the thinking_longer fact in agent.ts), with d1109-chat-recall's "Should I look for it?" as the other trigger; a small fix area "chat-yes-to-own-question" would also fit
verdict.notes: The leftovers only touch this: C3L-8 (a stale app ask line, after another line has followed, makes a typed yes answer nothing) is the app-offer version of the same dead end, and LL-10 is about the language of YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY. Neither names a yes to the model's own question. Two model choices sit next to this finding but are not it: in c10-quote, Haiku never called recall and ended 8 of 20 replies with "Should I look…?", against the prompt's "Look it up before you say you do not have it". In d2 and e1 it never called answer_thoroughly. Those may be their own findings, but the dead end after a yes is the app's code, and the app's prompt (conversation-agent.md: "yes" refers to earlier replies) and the facts line make the question likely. Severity is major: it is the core chat journey, the question pattern is frequent with Haiku, and the reply contradicts the question just above it. The workaround (typing "yes, look it up") is not obvious. Repro file: /tmp/frbench/l4chat2/yes.test.ts with /tmp/frbench/l4chat2/vitest.config.ts. finding.title: The real chat model never calls answer_thoroughly; depth questions get quick answers or a hand-over announced in words only
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'make a plan for the next two sessions' got 'This is a plan question across several sessions, so I can hand it to the stronger model. It asks you first, since it costs more. Should I go ahead?' with no cost, no time and no Go ahead button. 'review the decisions for conflicts' got 'That is the only conflict I found' (colours), but the recorded decisions 'No photos of members' (14 Nov) and gallery 'Yes, with their names' (15 Nov) conflict too. The failure question with the failed-task card waiting never gets 'This needs a stronger model: ... Go ahead?'.
finding.expected: LC-C13: answer_thoroughly on at least 3 of the 4 depth lines. The C3 fix-up: the failure question in a project with a failed task and a waiting card gets the stronger model's ask line with Go ahead.
finding.evidence: c13.json and c13c.json: answer_thoroughly called 0 of 4 times on depth lines and 0 of 3 times on the failure question (d1, r1, r2). It was offered in every call's tools. The only ask line came from the explicit 'use a stronger model:' prefix (e3). Plan question announced in words twice (d2, e1). The d1 answer itself was correct (task_get; the cause from the reports; two next steps).
finding.repro: Seed Garden club (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/scripts/seed-c11-c13.mts) on bench-live, then in its Chat ask: 'why does "Write the welcome page" keep failing and what should I change?', 'make a plan for the next two sessions', 'compare the last two sessions', 'review the decisions for conflicts'.
finding.suspected_cause: The hand-over depends on the fast model choosing the tool. Haiku at effort low answers alone or describes the hand-over in text. No app-side detection of depth questions on the default path.

verdict.root_cause:
On the default path, the only thing that can start a hand-over is the fast model picking answer_thoroughly. That model is Haiku 5.5 at effort low with thinking disabled (agent.ts:1813), with 37 tools and a role prompt that opens "You answer fast and short from what you are given" (conversation-agent.md:14). The app never notices a depth question on its own, by design (ADR 0114 "Who decides": no keyword routing beyond the person's phrases). Code alone does not prove the model will never call the tool. What the code does explain is the brief making the wrong choice likely on every C13 line.

In Garden club the failed task's card is listed in full, so turn.recordsRead is set. agent.ts:1711-1721 therefore writes "- thinking_longer: asks the person first" into # Now on every typed turn there. This is confirmed in the logged requests for d1, d2, d4 and r1 (model-calls.jsonl rows 46, 48, 52, 57). The tool's definition (depth.ts:332) ends "The facts' thinking_longer line says whether it is available now." That line has no subject (depth.ts:376), so it reads as an instruction to the model: ask the person first, in words, instead of calling the tool. The real replies repeat it almost word for word: d2 "...so I can hand it to the stronger model. It asks you first, since it costs more. Should I go ahead?" and e1 "This plan needs the stronger model, which costs more and asks you first. Should I go ahead?". No tool was called, so no offer was stored, and the typed "yes" got "Yes to what?". On the failure lines (d1, r1, r2) and on d4 the model just answered from the card and the history.

Evidence that this is not a test artefact: the API request body (creds/c25-proxy/bodies/4-req.json) carries answer_thoroughly with its full definition and its enum schema. Across all 76 logged chat calls in c1, not one reply calls it. Only the person's own phrases ("use a stronger model:", "think it through:") and the Think it through button ever went deeper.

The stand-in cannot show this. role-player.ts:1673-1681 and :1710-1716 call answer_thoroughly from a regex on exactly these lines ("keep failing", "compare", "plan for/the next", "review", "last two sessions"). The composed test chat-depth.test.ts:1135-1160 scripts the FakeProvider to call it too. So every acceptance test for the need-based hand-over passes against a model behaviour the real fast model does not show, and no eval covers conversation-agent (evals/registry/evals has only coder and researcher).

Severity is major. The owner's D3 ("escalates effort or model selectively ... when the question needs it") and U-094's Check in the app fail on the default setting: 0 of 4 depth lines and 0 of 3 failure questions handed over. The plan question shows a "Should I go ahead?" with no button, and a "yes" to it is answered "Yes to what?". The review question gets an incomplete answer: it missed the photos-versus-gallery conflict. It is not a blocker: the quick answers to d1 and d3 were correct, and the explicit phrases and the Think it through button work.

1) Words, so the model is never the one who asks:
- Make thinking_longer's "asks" value say who acts, e.g. "available: call answer_thoroughly; the app asks the person with the cost (never ask in your own words)".
- Drop "says whether it is available now" from ANSWER_THOROUGHLY_DESCRIPTION. Add: "Never offer a stronger model or ask 'Should I go ahead?' yourself: call this tool; the app writes the ask."

2) An app-side backstop (an ADR 0114 amendment, since the ADR rules out keyword routing):
- Move the stand-in's need patterns into depth.ts as needOfLine(text) → Why | null. Cover why ... fail(ed)/keep(s) failing, a plan for/the next, compare, review ... for, the last two/three sessions, and German siblings.
- When a typed quick pass ends without answer_thoroughly and needOfLine finds a need, run the tool's gate in code: spoken, quick, injection, room, rung, the ask rule. A lookup by the quick pass does not refuse here, because the offer spends nothing.

3) Add a stand-in mode in which the fast model answers alone on depth lines, so the backstop is tested at the bench boundary. Add a conversation-agent eval of LC-C13's 4 depth and 4 quick lines for the live check.

finding.title: The stronger model's answer says it could not use the stronger model, under a footer saying it did
finding.what_the_person_sees: After 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.29 (at most CHF 0.57) and 30 seconds. Go ahead?' and Go ahead: 'Here's a plan from the tasks as they stand. I couldn't hand it to the stronger model, so this comes from what I have. Nothing has changed. ...' with the footer 'Thought it through with Sonnet · 6 s · CHF 0.04'.
finding.expected: The paid thorough answer reads as the thorough answer. It never claims the stronger model was not used (design §5 rule 9: no promises the code does not keep).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png. Model-call log 06:20:25.572Z: claude-sonnet-5-5, medium, USD 0.048816, no tool calls, no lookup. Its system still holds '## Thinking longer: answer_thoroughly hands a question to a stronger model' while the tool is not offered. Its facts say 'thinking_longer: asks the person first'. Its history ends with Haiku's 'This plan needs the stronger model ... Should I go ahead?', 'yes', 'Yes to what?'.
finding.repro: Garden club Chat: 'make a plan for the next two sessions', 'yes', then 'use a stronger model: make a plan for the next two sessions', then press Go ahead.
finding.suspected_cause: The thorough pass reuses the quick turn's system section about handing over, and its facts line, without saying it is the stronger model. The earlier hand-over talk in history then leads it to deny the hand-over.

verdict.root_cause:
After the person presses Go ahead, the thorough pass gets a request that tells the stronger model nothing about who it is. Several parts of that request point it toward "the hand-over did not happen":
(1) The facts say `thinking_longer: asks the person first`. That line was worked out for this turn's quick pass (agent.ts:1706-1722), and the thorough pass reuses the same `volatile` (agent.ts:1829, thoroughRequest(volatile)). So it is no longer true once the person has said yes, which breaks design §5 rule 4 "True now" for status text given to the chat model.
(2) On an accepted offer, the question is the offer's question (agent.ts:1412). The last message is therefore the question again plus the facts (agent.ts:1645-1648), sitting right after the history's "This needs a stronger model: … Go ahead?". The person's "Go ahead." never appears anywhere the model can see it.
(3) The system part is the full role prompt, including "## Thinking longer: `answer_thoroughly` hands a question to a stronger model … when it answers 'Not now' or 'Not yet', answer briefly from what you have" (evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:49-57). This is on purpose, for cache sharing, and asserted in chat-depth.test.ts:924. But the thorough tool list has no answer_thoroughly, and CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES (depth.ts:359) only says "This question was handed to you to think through". It never says "you are the stronger model the person said yes to" or "answer_thoroughly is not yours".
The live request (model-calls.jsonl line 54, claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium effort, 36 tools without answer_thoroughly, no tool calls) carries all three. The reply echoes the role prompt's refusal wording ("this comes from what I have"), so the app's brief made this choice likely. It is not the model on its own. Earlier Haiku turns in the history ("I can hand it to the stronger model … Should I go ahead?", then "yes" answered with "Yes to what?") made it worse. Those are separate quick-pass findings. The run C plan said the thorough pass "reuses the facts the fast pass built" and never covered the stale line. No test checks what a thorough request says about the pass itself, because the composed tests script the replies.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1722 (volatile carries the quick pass's thinking_longer) and :1829 (the thorough pass reuses it); agent.ts:1631-1648 (thoroughRequest: role prompt with '## Thinking longer' + CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES; messages = history + question); agent.ts:1412 (an accepted offer's question replaces 'Go ahead.', so the yes is never shown); packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:359 (CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES does not say it is the closer look / stronger model the person chose); evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:49-57
verdict.fix_sketch:
Give the thorough pass its own true facts, and say in its rules who it is.
(a) In thoroughPass, build the pass's volatile by replacing the thinking_longer line with a pass line. For example `withNowFact(context.volatile, "this_answer", thoroughFact(...))`, giving "- this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to (at most CHF 0.57)", or "the longer look on this model". Say "the person pressed Go ahead" when the pass is an accepted offer. Never send "asks the person first" to a pass that is already running. Put the sentence in depth.ts next to thinkingLongerFact and assert it verbatim.
(b) Extend CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES (depth.ts:359). It sits in the system part, so it stays cache-stable across thorough passes. Add something like: "You are that closer look: the stronger model or longer effort the app chose or the person said yes to. answer_thoroughly and the 'Thinking longer' section are the quick pass's, not yours. Never say you could not hand it over or that a stronger model was not used."
(c) Optionally, scope the role prompt's "## Thinking longer" to "on the quick pass, when the tool is offered" (bump conversation-agent.md to 1.4.1 and update the verbatim test).
Keep the fast request byte-identical (the R-chatcache tests).
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Composed, in packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts, at the model-request boundary: chat "use a stronger model: make a plan for the next two sessions", then w.chat("Go ahead.", { offer }). Take the one fake-sonnet thorough request. Its last message must NOT contain "- thinking_longer: asks the person first" and must contain the pass line (e.g. "- this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to"). Its system must end with the extended CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES saying it is the closer look and that answer_thoroughly is not its tool. A sibling case does the same for a quick-pass hand-over that went ahead (why: plan) and for Think it through (longer rung: "on this model"). Today the first assertion fails: the live request at 06:20:25.572Z carries the stale line.
For the person's boundary, add an LC-C13 live-check step: after Go ahead on the stronger-model ask, the answer never says the stronger model was not used, and the footer names Sonnet.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes:
Confirmed against the real request in /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, line 54 (seq at 06:20:25.572Z, runId 01a1e829-f24b-…:thorough). The bench setup.log ties this run to 4cf11fd.

finding.title: Recall's card hit leaves out what the card asked, so chat says the record does not say it
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'It is not clearly about a first page, and it is no longer open. No card about the first page was found, and nothing in the records says what the writer asked there.' The card asked 'Which recipes go on the first page?'.
finding.expected: A card's hit line carries its question (as recall_open's 'It asked: ...' does), so a recall-only answer can say what was asked.
finding.evidence: Model-call log, the tool result for recall {words:'card first page', kinds:[cards, conversation]}: 'r6 [card, Mon 16 Nov, Recipe site, weak] "Write the index page" needs your answers: You answered "your answers". Answer: The three soups. (you)'. recall_open of the same card shows 'It asked: The writer asks: Which recipes go on the first page? ...'.
finding.repro: Recipe site Chat (seed-c11-c13.mts): 'look it up: what did the writer ask on the card about the first page, and what did we say about that card?'
finding.suspected_cause: The cards kind of recall builds the hit from the card's title and outcome, not its question.

verdict.root_cause: cardHits builds a card hit's visible line from the Inbox title plus `detail`, and `detail` holds only the Answered outcome and the answer (recall.ts:707-720). The search line prints the title and then a snippet of `r.detail ?? r.body` (recall.ts:1528). Because `detail` is set, the body is never shown. That body holds r.why and r.steps, which are the words the hit matched on. For a questions card (person_questions:*), the title is '"X" needs your answers' or '"X": the specialist asks you' (request-words.ts:559), so the title never names the question either. cardAnswerWords drops the question when the card has one question: `if (pairs.length === 1) return pairs[0]?.chosen` (recall.ts:347). With several questions it does print "Q A; Q A". So the search can find a one-question card by its question, but the hit line never shows the question. Only recall_open shows it ('It asked: ...', recall.ts:736). The base pins this behaviour: chat-recall.test.ts:963 expects the Bakery hit '"Ask for the opening hours" needs your answers: Answers saved ...; Answer: Mon to Fri 9 to 18.' with no 'What are the opening hours?'. I ran that test at 4cf11fd and it passes. In the live turn (model-call seq 7) the hit was r6, weak, and nothing in its line said "first page". The model judged it 'not clearly about a first page' and did not open it.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/recall.ts:720 (detail without the question; title at :703, single-answer words at :347, hit line from detail at :1528)
verdict.fix_sketch: In cardHits, when the card's title does not carry its question (questions cards, whose title is '"X" needs your answers' or '"X": the specialist asks you'), start `detail` with the question(s). Use the same words as recall_open: `It asked: ${r.steps.map(withoutNoActionGiven).map(oneLine).join(" | ")}`, cut to about 120 characters. Then put the outcome and 'Answer: ...' after it. snippetOf then centres on the matched words ("first page"). Keep the generic card unchanged: its title already is the question ('Where is the page published?'). Optionally have the hit print the pair as 'Q → A' for a one-question card instead of only A. finding.repro: Quote Page Chat: 'what did I say about the pizza oven?', 'when did we decide on the newsletter?'

verdict.root_cause:
The finding matches the model-call log (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl seq 17 and 18). Both control turns ran on claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low with thinking off. recall and recall_open were among the tools sent, yet each turn made one call with no tool call and ended normally (end_turn). The app did as designed: recall was offered, and CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) plus conversation-agent.md:46 say to look it up before saying you do not have it. The model chose not to. The app's own text still made that choice likely, and no code catches it:
(1) conversation-agent.md:68 says "If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through". That gives the model a sanctioned way out without any lookup, and its replies use exactly that form ("in Quote Page's tasks, the last session or the files I have"). Line 14 adds "You answer fast and short from what you are given."
(2) The 12-turn history (transcript.ts:267 HISTORY_TURNS) replays the model's own earlier offers. Those offers began at p2 ("I can search the records for it") and p6 ("I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look...?"). By c1 the history held 3 such replies and by x4 it held 6. Every miss after p6 copies the wording almost word for word. The base tendency is still the model's own: p2 skipped the lookup with no such history, and Recipe site seq 3 did the same. Bakery, with an empty history, called recall 2 of 2 times.
(3) Nothing in code checks for this. The claim guard (agent.ts:2028-2095, claimOf in claims.ts:139) catches only false change or ask claims. A reply that says it lacks something, or asks "Should I look?", without a recall call in the turn goes to the person unchanged.
The "guess" happened in c1 only ("probably in the Bakery project, which has two open cards"). It is a hedged guess built on the facts line "+2 cards in Bakery", and it is the model's own doing. The step expects Bakery to be named only after looking there. c2 guessed nothing and neither reply invented a record. This does not reproduce on the stand-in bench: role-player.ts:1645-1662 always calls recall for a PAST_RE line and returns "Looked through:". Same cause as L4-chat-1.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:68 (and :14); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2028 (claim guard only, no lookup check); agent.ts:617 (CHAT_RECALL_RULES); packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:267
verdict.fix_sketch:
1) Prompt (conversation-agent.md 1.4.x and CHAT_RECALL_RULES, both asserted verbatim):
- Replace line 68 with: "When the first message does not hold what the person asks about, call recall before you answer; if it finds nothing, say what it looked through."
- Add: "A lookup reads only and needs no yes: never offer to look something up or ask whether to, just look." and "Never say where something probably is (another project) without looking; use recall with project 'all'."
2) Code guard next to the claim guard (agent.ts ~2028): add missOf(text) in claims.ts. It matches lacks-or-offers wording ("can't find|don't have|haven't searched|no record|Should I (look|search)|I can search"). The guard fires when the turn's runs made no recall call, recall is in the tools, the run completed and calls are left (CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS 6). It then sends one nudge step, without streaming its text: "You have not looked this up. Call recall with the person's words and other words for it, then answer from what it returns." As the claim guard does, it resets the live bubble with CHECKING_STEP and the "Looking through everything recorded…" step line. With no call left, the reply stays. The nudge runs inside the turn's call room and budget, and the claim guard runs after it.
3) That breaks the history loop: once each miss runs a lookup, the history stops filling with "Should I look?" offers, so the history itself needs no change.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-recall (model-facing recall text and conversation-agent.md); the miss guard sits beside l3-chat-claims' claim guard in agent.ts
verdict.notes: Agree minor. Both replies are honest: they say they have not searched and invent no record. The person needs one more line, and a plain "yes" to the model's offer gets "Yes to what?", which belongs to a separate finding. The finding's "a guess" applies to c1 only. CL-11 mentions that LC-C10 watches the real model's choice, but it is about recall ranking, not about whether the model calls recall, so no leftover names this. verdict.root_cause:
The finding has two causes, and the code at 4cf11fd explains both.
(1) Chat 'summary'. The typed 'summary' is answered by the summary.speak command, not by the model: chatWhat in c31f.json shows the model was at its limit and did not answer. The command's chatProjectSummary reads the stored summary_cache.last_session.summary as written (packages/commands/src/commands/summary.ts:79). The chat and voice text path reads it the same way through textOf and spokenProjectSummary (summary.ts:46). Neither goes through resultAfterWait (packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-indicator.ts:60). That function is the C3-left-8 rule that turns '; then your session goes on.' into '; then it runs at your next Start.' once nothing is kept. It runs only in the daemon, for the session page (server.ts:2139), the Overview view and its Read aloud (views.ts:426, used by POST /projects/:id/speak), and the Inbox Update line (server.ts:2475). The commands package has no port to it. The chat model's project facts are not rewritten either (packages/runtime/src/conversation/project-facts.ts:157).
(2) The Overview until reload. The daemon's projectSummary view is already right after Cancel; the afterReset capture shows the new words after navigating. finding.title: Go ahead under 'This needs a stronger model' only asks again: the stronger model never runs
finding.what_the_person_sees: The person asks 'use a stronger model: why did "Build the contact form" fail and what should I change?' and gets 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?'. Each press of Go ahead (and a typed 'yes') adds 'Go ahead.' and the identical line again with a new Go ahead button. Nothing else happens, however often they press.
finding.expected: Go ahead runs the stronger model once on the question, within the 'at most' it showed, and the answer ends with 'Thought it through with Sonnet · … s · CHF …'.
finding.evidence: c14.json turn y1 plus c14b-goahead1/2.json and c14c.json: 0 model calls, replies in 95-376 ms. Screenshot 60-c14c-01-y2yes.png shows four identical ask lines. The stored offers' atMostUsdMicro grow each turn: 206,334 -> 208,455 -> 208,905 -> 209,205 -> 209,505, with estimateUsdMicro 48,816 (the median of the one earlier Sonnet pass, LC-C13 e3). With 'Chat asks first' at CHF 0 the longer rung's Go ahead did run, because its 'at most' (twice the estimate) is above the floor. So did the best rung's ('at most CHF 1.13').
finding.repro: On the c1 home (one cheap Sonnet answer, USD 0.0488, already in the conversation), in any project's Chat: type 'use a stronger model: why did "<a failed task>" fail and what should I change?' and press Go ahead under the ask. The same ask line comes back. Press again or type 'yes': same.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1872. personsPass re-asks when yes.atMostUsdMicro < f.floorUsdMicro. The floor is PASS_FLOOR_CALLS (3) x the first call's worst case on the current context (line 1666), and that context now includes the ask turn itself, so it is a little larger each time. 'at most' = max(2 x estimate, floor) (atMostOf). Once a recent stronger pass cost less than half the floor, 'at most' equals the old floor exactly, and every later floor is bigger. Because the estimate is the median of recent passes across the one conversation session that all projects share, every stronger-model Go ahead on the install loops until 200 newer chat replies push that pass out of recentPasses.

verdict.root_cause: The re-ask check compares the yes against an internal number that is always a little lower than the new floor. Go ahead is never handled as a yes. atMostOf (packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:166-173) returns max(twice the estimate rounded up to the centime, floor), and when the floor is larger it returns the floor in micro-USD without rounding. That happens whenever the estimate (recentPasses' median, agent.ts:1667-1669) is less than half the floor, which is PASS_FLOOR_CALLS x the first call's worst case (agent.ts:1666). The offer stores that unrounded value (offerOf, agent.ts:1700-1708). On the Go ahead turn, personsPass (agent.ts:1864-1872) works out the floor again with figuresOf on thoroughRequest. Its history now holds the offered turn itself (the question and the ask line), so the floor is a few hundred micro-USD larger. yes.atMostUsdMicro < f.floorUsdMicro is then always true, and a fresh offer with the same line is stored. That offer's 'at most' is the new floor, which the next turn's floor exceeds again, and so on without end. The re-ask has no reason to fire. The person was shown chfUp(atMost) = CHF 0.17 (USD 0.2125 at 0.8), and every later floor (208,455 to 209,505) still fits inside that figure. So running would not spend past anything the person was shown; the check compares against the unrounded internal value, not the shown one. It persists across the install: conversationSession is keyed by the agent only (agent.ts:2734-2735), so every project shares one session, and recentPasses reads the newest 200 chat.reply rows (event.ts:88-101, newest first). A single cheap stronger pass therefore makes every later stronger Go ahead loop, since no new stronger pass can run to move the median. Confirmed from the c1 store: offers on the same question with estimate 48,816 and atMost 205,890 -> 206,334 -> 208,455 -> 208,905 -> 209,205 -> 209,505, none followed by a Sonnet pass. Reproduced at 4cf11fd with the composed chat (real LoopAgentDriver, CommandLoop, FakeProvider, flatPricing; test at /tmp/frbench/v-l4chat12/t/repro.test.ts). With no seed, or a seeded fake-sonnet pass of 100,000, Go ahead runs fake-sonnet. With a seeded pass of 1,000, three Go aheads give the identical line 'about CHF 0.01 (at most CHF 0.04)' and zero model calls, with stored atMost 39,339 -> 39,519 -> 39,639 -> 39,759. The longer rung's Go ahead in c14d ran only because twice its estimate (12,500) was above its floor.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1872 (the re-ask); causes at packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:172 (atMostOf returns the floor unrounded) and agent.ts:1666-1674 (the floor is measured on a context that the offer turn has grown); the same comparison again at agent.ts:1889
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Make the stored 'at most' the figure the person reads: atMostOf rounds the max up to the centime, i.e. chfToUsdMicroAt(centimesUp(max(2*estimate, floor), chf)/100, chf), so the budget a yes carries equals the CHF on the line. 2) In personsPass, judge a yes against what was shown: re-ask only when the model changed or centimesUp(f.floorUsdMicro) > centimesUp(yes.atMostUsdMicro). The pass then runs with budget = yes.atMostUsdMicro, capped by the room as today. Apply the same change to the duplicate check at agent.ts:1889. 3) Optional: measure an accepted offer's floor without the offered turn's own ask line in the history, so the figures on the accept turn match the ones that turn offered. A re-ask after a real price change or model change (the documented restart case) stays as it is, and the new figure is shown.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts (composed chat, fake-haiku fast pass, fake-sonnet stronger): seed one chat.reply row with a stronger pass {depth: 'stronger', model: 'fake-sonnet', costUsdMicro: 1_000}, in another project of the same agent. Send 'use a stronger model: <QUESTION>' and expect the ask line and no model call. Send 'Go ahead.' with offer: r.transcriptId and expect exactly one fake-sonnet request. Its reply's footer should match /^Thought it through with Sonnet · \d+ s · /, its cost should be at most the CHF 'at most' on the line, and no second ask row should be written. Today it fails: zero requests and the same ask line, with the row's atMostUsdMicro growing on each press. Do the same through the daemon's chat route with the stand-in, and on the UI's Go ahead button: the conversation shows one answer under Go ahead, not a second ask.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes: The evidence supports every part of the claim. The c14 step files show 0 calls on each Go ahead and on the typed 'yes' (95-376 ms). The copied c1 store (/tmp/frbench/v-l4chat12/state.sqlite) holds the offers and their figures as the finding says; the first ask had atMost 205,890 and the Go ahead under it stored 206,334. The cheap pass is the LC-C13 Sonnet pass (48,816). The earlier 'make a plan' Go ahead ran because there was no median yet (estimate = 5 x worst). The best rung ran because no Opus pass had been recorded yet; one cheap Opus pass would make it loop too. The model's own hand-over (answer_thoroughly -> ask) goes through the same accept path, so its Go ahead loops in the same way. Nothing is spent and nothing goes wrong beyond the loop, so I keep major rather than blocker. Still, after the first cheap stronger answer, the stronger and best rungs that the owner's decision D3.2 promises cannot be used anywhere on the install. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this (C3L-8 is about stale ask lines and C3L-13 about the turn floor; neither is this). c16b.json reply: '... which conflicts with these records.

This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?

Thought it through more carefully · 5 s · under CHF 0.01'. Screenshot 76-c16c-after-restart.png.

verdict.root_cause: The app cannot tell the person's Answer now apart from the budget's wrap-up. Answer now is wired as `entry.answerNow = () => budget.wrapUpNow(o.runId)` (agent.ts:1776). `SessionBudget.wrapUpNow` (enforcement/budget.ts:283) adds the run to `wrapNow`. `precheck` then sets `wrap = ... (runSpent + lineEstimate > line.lineUsdMicro || this.wrapNow.has(runId))` (budget.ts:266-270): both causes end in the same `line.wrapped` and the same `wrap_up` decision. The loop sets `wrapUpSent = true` either way (agent/loop.ts:712). After the answer, agent.ts:2253 adds the next rung's ask line on `deep && !stopped && result?.wrapUpSent && !offer` alone, so an answer the person cut short gets 'This needs a stronger model … Go ahead?'. ADR 0114 ("their yes under a stronger answer that ran out of room"), runtime.md:4436 and the runC plan say this offer belongs only under an answer whose budget ran out. In the evidence the budget was not the cause: the pass's first call cost USD 0.001046 against a budget of about USD 0.125 (CHF 0.10), far below the 85% line, so the wrap-up came only from the press (the c16b stopRequests show POST /chat/turns/…/answer-now at 08:52:46.445).

"line" : "now"`) and expose `wrapReasonOf(runId)`. The loop or the agent then reads it, and agent.ts:2253 becomes `deep && !stopped && result?.wrapUpSent && budget.wrapReasonOf(runId) === "line" && !offer`. Smaller option, agent-only: in runOf, `entry.answerNow = () => { const ok = budget.wrapUpNow(o.runId); if (ok) answeredNow = true; return ok; }` and add `!answeredNow` to the condition. A press after the budget already wrapped returns false and keeps the offer, which is correct. With either option, the Answer-now reply carries no offer and stores none on the chat.reply row. finding.title: Thorough answers take back correct earlier statements without looking them up
finding.what_the_person_sees: After Go ahead on a closer look: 'My earlier answer also gave a date and a file name (map.html, Sunday 15 November). I can't confirm those from the records I have now, so rely on the empty places file as the cause.' (0 lookups). In Garden club: 'I need to correct my earlier answers. I said the Sunday session wrote a placeholder list that the critic rejected, and that the welcome page failed on Friday too. The records I just read don't show that, so I can't confirm it.' All of these statements were true in the run reports and session records.
finding.expected: A thorough pass looks up what it doubts (recall_open of the session or report) before calling an earlier answer wrong, as CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES asks ('Look up what the answer rests on').
finding.evidence: c14d-goahead.json: 1 Haiku call, text only. c15.json k3: recall + session_last only, no recall_open. Seeded report of 15 Nov: 'I wrote a placeholder list, but the critic sent it back'. Session of 13 Nov: 'Write the welcome page' failed.
finding.repro: Photo club: 'think it through: why did "Add the meeting map" fail ...' then, with Chat asks first at CHF 0, ask it again and press Go ahead. Garden club: after earlier failure answers, 'think it through: what did the last two sessions do?'.
finding.suspected_cause: Model behaviour, helped by L4-chat-15 (recall's session record leaves out the failure). In Garden club, session_last also said 'no session yet' because the seed did not write the project's last-session summary (a seed artifact, not reported).

verdict.root_cause:
The two cases have different causes.

C15 (Garden club, k3): the code explains it. The model did look things up (recall kinds=sessions, then session_last). The records it got back were incomplete in a way that read as complete. sessionGist (session-list.ts:215-219) returns only "Did N tasks: <done titles>." when any task was done, so the failed task drops out. The recall hit also shows `detail` (gist + "How it ended" + cost, recall.ts:427-444 and 1528), never the session row's own summary. That summary did say '"Write the welcome page" failed' and '"Write the welcome page" failed again'. The tool result in model-calls.jsonl line 67 reads 'Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Done.' for Fri 13 Nov, and the same pattern for Sun 15 Nov. The model then "corrected" two earlier statements that were true. session_last saying "has had no session yet" is a seed artifact: seed-c11-c13.mts:57 left summary_cache {}, and lastSessionBlock (project-facts.ts:173-177) reads that cache, which a real session end writes. This is the root cause of the sibling finding L4-chat-15. recall_open (sessionText, recall.ts:452-470) and task_get would have shown the failures, but nothing in the hit hinted they were missing.

C14d (Photo club, Go ahead at CHF 0): the model alone. The Go ahead pass had the same system prompt and the same 36 tools as the first thorough pass x1, which called task_get (I compared lines 60 and 64 of model-calls.jsonl: system and tools are identical). The only difference was the history, which held its own earlier answer to the same question. It made 0 tool calls, answered from the facts' "Failed: data/places.csv has no rows", and called its earlier map.html and 15 Nov details unconfirmed. finding.title: Once a conversation passes 12 turns, each chat turn writes its history to the cache again
finding.what_the_person_sees: Nothing on screen. Each quick turn pays the cache-write price on the whole history (about 1,900-2,000 tokens per turn on Haiku here; more on Sonnet thorough passes).
finding.expected: cache_read_input_tokens covers tools, system and history on quick turns 2 and 4 (spec of LC-C15).
finding.evidence: c15.json: k2 read 16,128, wrote 1,915; k4 read 16,128, wrote 2,028; k1 wrote 17,988. Every quick request carries 25 messages, and the first person line differs on each turn ('what did we decide about the colours?', 'why did "Write the welcome page" fail three times...', 'compare the last two sessions'), with 0 identical leading messages between k1 and k2.
finding.repro: In a project whose chat has more than 12 turns, send two quick lines within 5 minutes and compare reply.usage in the model-call log.
finding.suspected_cause: The history window is the last 12 turns and slides by one each turn, so the prefix after the system part never matches the previous request's cache breakpoint. A window that moves in steps (or a breakpoint before the newest turns) would keep it.

verdict.root_cause:
The chat's history is a window over the newest turns, and it moves by one turn every turn. historyMessages keeps `turns.slice(-HISTORY_TURNS)` (12 turns). If those turns are over the token budget, it drops the oldest turns one at a time until they fit (`build(from)`). So once a conversation has more than 12 turns, or its history is over the budget, every request starts with a different first message. The prompt cache matches by prefix, so the request matches the previous one only through tools and system. Each turn then writes the whole history to the cache again.

The model-call log shows this: k1, k2 and k4 each carry 25 messages, and no leading message is the same between k1 and k2 or between k3 and k4. k2 and k4 each read 16,128 tokens (tools + system only) and wrote 1,915 and 2,028.

The adapter's breakpoints are right. cacheHistory marks the last message's stable start, and the earlier line of wave 7 (R-chatcache, the now-facts kept out of the line) works. A read-only repro with testenv's PromptCacheSim and the real historyMessages, in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-chat-16/repro.mts, confirms both cases:
- 4 to 5 prior turns: turn B reads 2,720 tokens (tools + system + history) and writes 59.
- 13 to 14 and 20 to 21 prior turns: turn B reads only 2,462 (tools + system) and writes 741 and 755.

The thorough pass builds its history the same way (THOROUGH_HISTORY_TOKENS 8,000), so it has the same slide.

Existing tests miss this because they only use short conversations: conversation.test.ts:1312-1345 and chat-depth.test.ts:887-917.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:379 (const recent = turns.slice(-HISTORY_TURNS)), with :396-400 (the token-cap loop drops the oldest turns one by one) and HISTORY_TURNS at :267; called from packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1605-1607 (quick pass) and :1630 (thorough pass)
verdict.fix_sketch:
Make the start of the window stable and move it in steps, not by one turn each turn. Work out the first turn from facts that do not depend on which turn is asking, for example the turn's index from the start of the conversation (seq or a count, not the position inside the 100-turn read), rounded down to a step of K turns (K = 6):
- start = max(0, floor((n - HISTORY_TURNS) / K) * K)
- The window then holds 12 to 12+K-1 turns and moves forward only every K turns.

Treat the token cap the same way. When the turns are over the budget, drop the oldest turns in blocks anchored to the same start (or keep the start until the budget plus a margin is passed), never one turn per call. The result must stay a pure function of the stored rows, so it is also the same after a restart.

The finding's other idea, a breakpoint before the newest turns, would not help: the change is at message 0, and a prefix cache cannot read anything after the first difference. Carrying up to K more turns is cheap, because they are read at 0.1x the input price instead of written at 1.25x. Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md ('History') to describe the stepped window.

Seed a conversation of 13 turns, or chat 13 lines. Then send two quick lines within 5 minutes on the simulated clock. Check the two requests in the model-call log:

- The second request's cache_read_input_tokens is greater than what tools + system alone are worth (billed as in conversation.test.ts:1331-1337), and covers the first request's history.

finding.title: Chat asks for a yes in words with no Yes/No card; the person's 'yes' gets 'Yes to what?'; the reply guard never fires
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'This widens what research may read, so I need your yes first. Shall I set research for Reading rules to any public website again?' with no buttons. A typed 'yes' gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' The rule stays 'only developer.mozilla.org'. Project C did the same twice in a row.
finding.expected: A Yes/No read-back on the first try. If the model answers in text only, the reply should be 'Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.'
finding.evidence: Card on the first try in 1 of 3 fresh projects; the guard line appears 0 times in /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/daemon.log. In the model-call log the first-try calls have toolCalls [] and that text (claude-haiku-5-5). Screenshots: l3b/steps/09-rr1-t3-reply.png, 10-rr1-t3b-reply.png, 25-reading-rules-c-t3-reply.png, 28-reading-rules-c-t3c-reply.png.
finding.repro: New project; in Chat say 'only read developer.mozilla.org for research', then 'research may read any public website again', then 'yes'; repeat on two fresh projects.
finding.suspected_cause: The guard looks for claims that a change was made or a yes was asked. It does not catch a question that asks for the yes itself when no command ran. Sibling of L4-session-2.

verdict.root_cause: The model (claude-haiku-5-5, low effort) answered the widening request in text and called no tool. The model-call log at /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl shows this at seq 3, 14 and 15: toolCalls [], replies "...so I need your yes first. Shall I set research ... again?" and "...it needs your yes first. Should research ... be allowed to read any public website again?". The prompt does tell it to call the command, so the slip starts with the model. But the app has a guard built for exactly this live failure (l3-chat-claims, from L3-run-1, which was the same request), and the guard does not see this phrasing. claimOf (packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:139) only matches past-tense claims about the app: ASKED at claims.ts:69-106 ("I've asked for confirmation", "I'm waiting for your yes", "I'll apply it once you approve"...) and CHANGED at :108-119. A reply that asks for the yes in words matches neither: no "Shall I / Should I / Do you want me to ...?" and no "(I|it) need(s) your yes". So falseClaim (agent.ts:2045-2050) returns null. I ran claimOf with tsx on all three live replies and it returned null each time, while the L3-run-1 sentence returned kind "asked". No nudge was sent: each of those turns has exactly one model call, and "chat reply claimed what no command did" appears 0 times in daemon.log. The person then types "yes", and the app catches it before the model (agent.ts:1214-1220). No card waits and the newest reply is no go_ahead offer (liveOffer, agent.ts:893), so nothingWaitingReply sends YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (agent.ts:527, 2600). That is the app contradicting the question it showed one line above. The prompt adds to the problem: conversation-agent.md:21 says '"yes" ... refer[s] to' the recent conversation, but a bare "yes" with nothing waiting never reaches the model, so asking in words looks answerable to the model when it is not. Rate: a card on the first try in 1 of 3 projects (project B, seq 10). Project C asked in text twice before a reworded line ("yes, let research read any public website") made the model call settings_set. Sibling: L4-session-2 ("Do you want me to start a session ...?").
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:69 (ASKED patterns; claimOf at :139), with packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2045 (falseClaim) and agent.ts:1214-1220 (bare yes -> YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY, :527)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) claims.ts: add a third claim kind, "asks", for a reply that asks the person for a yes in words. A sentence that is a question offering to make a change ("Shall I / Should I / Do you want me to / Want me to / Soll ich" followed by a change verb: set, change, widen, allow, start, add, raise...), or a sentence saying "(I|it|this) need(s) your yes|confirmation|approval (first|before)" next to such a question. Keep NEGATION and EARLIER as they are, and leave clarifying questions without a change verb alone ("Which project?"). 2) agent.ts falseClaim: count an "asks" claim as false when !did.asked. claimNudge gets a lead for it: "Your reply asks the person for a yes in words, but no command in this turn read a change back, and a typed yes reaches no one. If the person asked for a change, call its command now; the runtime reads it back with Yes and No. Otherwise answer again without asking for a yes." If the model still only asks after the nudge, trueLine gives NOTHING_CHANGED_REPLY / NOTHING_CHANGED_CARD_WAITS_REPLY as today. 3) A backstop at agent.ts:1214: when the newest reply was such an unbacked question (store a flag on the transcript reply, e.g. reply.askedInWords), a bare "yes" should not get "Yes to what?". Either pass the yes, with the earlier line, to the model (safe: any change still gets its own read-back) or say the true line ("Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more."). 4) conversation-agent.md: add "Never ask for a yes in words (\"Shall I ...?\"); call the command and the runtime asks with Yes and No". Fix line 21 so it no longer implies that a bare yes reaches the model. Bump the prompt version. The same fix covers L4-session-2.

finding.title: Chat replies describe the app's tool calls and copy the 'The app did:' history marker
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'The second call was refused only because the setting already matched.' (B); 'The app did: research for Reading rules C now reads only developer.mozilla.org ...' (C)
finding.expected: A plain confirmation with no internals (section 5 rule 6).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/reading-rules-b-t2.json (two settings_set calls in one turn), reading-rules-c-t2.json
finding.repro: Turn 2 of L4-l3-1 on fresh projects.
finding.suspected_cause: The history now carries 'The app did: ...', and Haiku copies it. Tool refusals are passed to the model and it repeats them.

verdict.root_cause: C ('The app did: research for Reading rules C now reads ...'): the history did not cause this. The model-call log /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, seq 12-13, shows C's turn had no history at all: messages holds only the person's line and the tool round. The marker came from the system prompt the app sends. That prompt says it twice, in words that read like a format for the reply: conversation-agent.md:21-22 says "A reply that changed something ends with the app's own line 'The app did: …'", and agent.ts:605 (CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES) says "An earlier reply's line 'The app did: …' is what that turn changed". Haiku then wrote the marker into its own reply. Nothing removes it afterwards. The reply text goes to the person as written, and replyInHistory (transcript.ts:353-366) keeps the model's prose next to the app's actionLines. So turn 3's history (seq 14) carries two "The app did:" lines for one change, and the model can no longer tell its own lines from the app's. B ('The second call was refused only because the setting already matched'): Haiku made two settings_set calls in one turn, one without the project and one with "Reading rules B". The first one applied. The second is a no-op: refuseNoChange (settings.ts:1078-1084) throws on it, and the tool layer sends it to the model as an error, content "Refused: … is already only developer.mozilla.org." with isError: true (registry.ts:215-218). The prompt then points the model at refusals: "when it is refused, read why and try again" (agent.ts:600-601) and "unless a tool answered … in this turn" (conversation-agent.md:86-88, agent.ts:603-605). No rule tells the model to keep its calls and tool results out of the reply. The same tool talk shows up elsewhere in the run: seq 16 'no tool has accepted a widening in this turn', seq 10 'the never list cleared'. Narrating its duplicate call is partly the model's own choice. The error-shaped no-op and the tool-centred prompt make it likely.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:21-22 and packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:605 (the prompt presents "The app did: …" as how a reply ends); packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:353-366 (replyInHistory keeps the model's own "The app did:" in the history); packages/commands/src/registry.ts:215-218 with packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:1078-1084 (a no-op set goes back as an is_error "Refused:")
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Prompt (conversation-agent.md, next version, and CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES): say that only the app writes the "The app did:" line, that it is never part of the model's own reply, and that the model never starts or ends a reply with it. Better still, take the marker out of the assistant content: give the history's changes as a facts block the app owns (for example "# Changed in this conversation"), so there is nothing in the model's own replies to copy. Under "How you answer", add: "Say what is true now for the person; never describe your tool calls, their order or their refusals." 2) Code: before a reply is shown and stored, remove a leading or embedded HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD from the model's text (in agent.ts, where finalText becomes the reply). In replyInHistory, also remove that lead from the prose, so the app's actionLines are the only lines that carry it. This keeps the rule "a reply without one changed nothing" true. 3) A no-op set (ForerunnerError details.unchanged) goes back as a plain tool result, not an error: "Nothing to change: <what> is already <value>." Optionally, when an earlier call in the same turn already made that exact change, the second identical settings_set call gets the same non-error answer, so there is no refusal for the model to talk about.
verdict.failing_test_idea: At the chat boundary (POST /chat on the composed runtime with a scripted model; conversation-memory.test.ts or a real-daemon.test.ts case): (a) On a fresh project's first turn the scripted model calls settings_set web_access only developer.mozilla.org, then answers "The app did: research for X now reads only developer.mozilla.org." Expect the reply text the person gets (ChatReplyView.text, the bubble) to contain no "The app did:". Expect the next turn's history assistant message to contain exactly one "The app did:" line, the app's own change sentence. Both fail today. (b) The scripted model calls settings_set twice in one turn, without and then with project, for the same value. Expect the second tool_result not to be is_error and not to start with "Refused:". This fails today. (c) Live eval, for the record: fresh project, Haiku, "only read developer.mozilla.org for research". The reply must not contain "The app did", "call", "tool" or "refused". It failed in 2 of 3 fresh projects in this run (B and C).
verdict.area_hint: small chat-words fix area. The code comes from run L3's l3-chat-claims (HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD, CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES, the prompt lines; runC-plan.json run_L3), and d1109-chat-guard is the closest run C chat area
verdict.notes: The finding's suspected cause is half wrong. The marker was not copied from the history: in project C the turn had no history (model-calls.jsonl seq 12-13, messages length 1), so the system prompt was the only source. The history does repeat it in later turns, though. Seq 14's history shows the model's line and the app's line, both starting "The app did:". Hidden risk, not observed in this run: the claim guard (claims.ts) only catches first-person claims ("I've set…"). A model that writes "The app did: …" on a reply that changed nothing gets past the guard, and that line enters the history looking like the app's own line, which breaks the rule the prompt gives ("a reply without it changed nothing"). Fix 2 closes this. B's duplicate call was the model's choice: two parallel settings_set calls, one with project and one without, both resolving to the active project. The app answered the second as an is_error refusal, and nothing in the prompt says to keep tool mechanics out of the reply. The facts in both replies are true and the Undo row is right, so I agree with severity words. I did not run the stand-in bench: its role-player scripts the chat model and cannot show what Haiku chooses. The code and the recorded requests explain the finding. No leftover names it; LL-10 (English-only correction lines) is a different issue.

Lessons of the closed project are not moved (ADR 0117's amendment: a lesson's file is canonical and carries its project). Chat recall reads them through withJoined, but the kept project's sessions do not get them in memory.

Guards on a closed project: POST /projects/:id/plan (applyProjectPlan, no UI client method) still writes milestones and tasks on it; the Data tab's Add and Import still accept data on it (unseen by the kept project); a chat change read back before the join and answered Yes after it runs from its prepared steps without the new guard (the guard is in prepare).

After Cancel on a waiting session, chat's project facts (packages/runtime/src/conversation/project-facts.ts) and the typed 'summary' command (packages/commands/src/commands/summary.ts:79) still read the stored last result as written, so chat can repeat '...; then your session goes on.'. run-indicator.ts resultAfterWait(store, projectId, since, text) is the one rule (daemon-only; the commands package needs it through a port).

The chat's own correction lines (NOTHING_CHANGED_REPLY, NOTHING_CHANGED_CARD_WAITS_REPLY, NO_ANSWER_REPLY, like 'Yes to what? …') are English only, so a German conversation gets an English line: whether the app's own chat lines follow the conversation's language is a decision.
